data.body:
Implementation landed as Gerrit change 2079 (patchset 2).

Mutation evidence — every new test was verified by perturbing the live implementation and confirming a specific test goes RED, then restoring:

| mutation | test that caught it |
|---|---|
| drop `--no-merges` from the log walk | `test_merge_commits_are_not_counted_as_prior_fixes` (3 != 2) |
| `REPEAT_FIX_MIN_PRIOR` 2 -> 1 | `test_a_single_prior_bug_fix_does_not_escalate` |
| `REPEAT_FIX_WINDOW_DAYS` 7 -> 70 | `test_prior_bug_fixes_outside_the_window_do_not_escalate` |
| count any resolvable ticket, not only `bug` | `test_prior_commits_on_a_non_bug_ticket_do_not_escalate` |
| tally priors across paths instead of per path | `test_priors_are_counted_per_path_not_across_paths` |
| ignore the `at` anchor (always "now") | `test_at_pins_the_window_to_a_point_in_time` |
| drop the repeat-fix arm of the OR | 4 gate tests incl. `test_both_signals_are_reported_together` |
| `non_test_paths_in_diff` keeps test paths | `test_non_test_paths_in_diff_drops_test_material` |
| blank `repeat_fix_priors` in coverage | `test_repeat_fix_escalates_an_under_floor_bug_fix` |
| teaching finding drops the priors clause | `test_the_teaching_finding_names_the_prior_fixes` |
| walk `HEAD` instead of `HEAD~1` | `test_the_change_under_review_is_not_counted_as_its_own_prior` |

The last one was a genuine defect found while implementing, not just a mutation: `assemble` builds the review diff as `HEAD~1..HEAD`, so in a review checkout HEAD IS the change under review. A first draft walked `HEAD`, which would have let a fix with a single genuine prior count itself as the second one and escalate on its own existence. Fixed by walking `HEAD~1` (the same base the diff is taken against) and pinned by the regression test above.

Ratchets: module-size 143 lines for the new module, `bugfix_size_gate.py` 392 of 800; `check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0 increased=0`.
